C-STABILIZE-SPLIT-DUAL-EDIT.Summary: The second Split View pane has been a read-only mirror since C-29 (NonGoal: "Simultaneous editing in both panes (mirror is read-only)"), which the owner reads as "editing does not work". The owner now directs full-quality dual editing and explicitly rejects the per-surface-undo compromise proposed in the retired draft C-SPLIT-VIEW-SYNC-EDIT (chat, 2026-10-27, translated: "Point 2 must be done fully and properly, so that editing works and everything works — otherwise it's crap"). This change makes both panes fully editable in split against the single store document, with one undo/redo history for the document regardless of which pane an edit was made in, per-surface carets that survive the other pane's commits, and every editor command working from the focused pane. The C-29 NonGoal is superseded by the owner decision of 2026-10-27; the archived spec stays byte-for-byte and this bundle records the supersession.

Goals.R-1: Both panes fully editable in split: typing, selections, clipboard (copy/cut/paste), drag-drop of text, IME composition, and image/text paste paths work in whichever pane has focus. The store remains the single document truth: a pane's own user edits commit through the existing paths (muya change listener; CodeMirror cursorActivity / LISTEN_FOR_CONTENT_CHANGE); the other pane re-renders render-only at the existing debounce (150 ms; muya's adaptive extension for heavy documents unchanged) under a rendering guard that generalizes the C-29 mirror guard from a static prop to a per-render state.
Goals.R-2: One document history — unified undo/redo. Cmd+Z in either pane reverts the document's last committed edit regardless of which pane made it; Cmd+Shift+Z / Cmd+Y redo mirrors it. Undo granularity follows commit coalescing (typing bursts coalesce as today). After every undo/redo step: both panes re-render from the store, the focused pane's caret and selection restore to the corresponding position in the reverted text (clamped), and the unfocused pane's remembered caret re-maps the same way. The undo stack is per tab, survives pane focus switches and mode toggles, and is cleared exactly when the document history is cleared today (tab switch, external reload).
Goals.R-3: Per-surface caret memory: each pane keeps its own caret and selection across the other pane's commits — positions translate and clamp into the updated text instead of jumping to the start; focus switching between panes never loses or moves the caret of the pane being entered. IME composition in the focused pane is never interrupted by the other pane's re-render (composition state fences re-renders of the composing surface only; the other pane still updates).
Goals.R-4: Command completeness — everything works from the focused pane: every editor command available in the current single-pane mode must work in split from whichever pane holds focus, and none may be silently a no-op. This includes at minimum: character and paragraph formatting (in the source pane they apply as equivalent text transforms), find & replace (match navigation and replacement target the focused surface), word count and document statistics, dirty state / autosave / problems panel, copy-as-structured-text, link and image insertion flows, and table/format-document operations. The plan ships a command-corner matrix enumerating every command id against both panes with verbatim expected behavior; a command that cannot meaningfully apply to a surface is explicitly listed as disabled with its visible reason, never silently dead.
Goals.R-5: Integrity invariants under two writers: exactly one dirty-flag move per user edit (no echo loops — the rendering guard is the boundary); muya normalization never rewrites source-pane edits (`*` bullets stay `*`); locked tabs (View › Lock Document) and Finder-preview read-only tabs keep BOTH panes read-only with selection/copy available; front-matter and encoding paths behave as today; word counting counts once.
Goals.R-6: Supersession bookkeeping: C-29's NonGoal "Simultaneous editing in both panes" is superseded by the owner decision of 2026-10-27, recorded here; the archived C-29 bundle is not edited. tests/e2e/ split-view.spec.ts mirror-read-only corners are rewritten into dual-edit corners (the `* item` normalization corner and the never-writes-back guard — now the rendering guard — keep passing).
Goals.R-7: Governance: history/caret/translation helpers are pure and unit-tested; the muya touch (if the approved architecture extends muya's commit path) is minimal, contract-updated, and enumerated in the plan; module/V-M anchors (new or M-011/V-M-011 extensions) are fixed by the plan after grace lint --parallel-preflight; graph and verification deltas route in the same bundle as the code.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Dual editing: typing in the rich pane updates the source pane within 300 ms and typing in the source pane updates the rich pane within 300 ms; both panes accept a caret, text selection, clipboard operations and IME input while split is on; edits from either pane mark the tab dirty, feed word count and autosave exactly once per edit.

Unified undo: with edits interleaved across panes (rich edit A, source edit B, rich edit C), Cmd+Z reverts C then B then A in document order regardless of which pane holds focus at undo time; redo replays them in order; after each step both panes show the reverted text and the focused pane's caret sits at the corresponding position; the stack survives pane focus switches and is cleared on tab switch/external reload as today.

Command matrix: every enumerated command id works from the focused pane (formatting, find/replace, insertion flows, statistics, copy-as-structured-text) or is explicitly disabled with a visible reason; the plan's matrix is fully covered by tests.

Integrity: the store keeps source-typed `* item` exactly after muya re-renders (normalization corner green); a locked tab leaves both panes read-only with copy available; no echo loops observable over sustained alternating edits.

Governance: pure helper unit suites (history routing, caret translation/clamping, guard state machine); rewritten and new e2e corners; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY updated in touched files including any muya file; graph and verification deltas routed with content-free markers; grace lint shows no new errors beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Cross-pane caret/selection visualization (seeing the other pane's caret); word-level diff or merge semantics between panes.
Collaborative editing, conflict resolution between simultaneous IME streams, or multi-document coupling.
Mobile/tablet split surfaces; split in Diff Mode; split below the 800px collapse.
Line-exact scroll mapping (C-SPLIT-SCROLL-SYNC owns proportional sync).

C-STABILIZE-SPLIT-DUAL-EDIT.IntegrationConstraint: Transplant product hunks only, retaining current page-width, progressive-mount, export and renderer behavior. Root applies all routed projections centrally; this worker changes no versions, release artifacts, commits or pushed refs.
C-STABILIZE-SPLIT-DUAL-EDIT.Decision: D-SPLIT-RECOVERY-02: delegated recovery representation accepted on 2026-11-09. For unified entries, store exactly one raw Markdown payload INSTEAD OF the existing block-tree clone, plus constant-size rich/source endpoint positions and focused-surface metadata. Do not store both document representations or selected text. Native pre-split content entries remain undoable; adjacent caret-only native entries collapse once at activation. Ordinary never-unified history and its public shape remain unchanged. Pending typing coalesces, and focus/command/tab boundaries commit it. Bounded storage and exact source replay are executable assertions.

D-SPLIT-RECOVERY-01: choose the stronger R-2/design-context/corner-10 behavior. A tab that entered unified split retains its muya-owned history and both translated carets/selections across tab switches and source/rich/split mode transitions. External content reload clears that unified state. The ambiguous original clear-on-tab-switch wording is superseded; ordinary never-unified single-pane semantics stay unchanged. Source native history is disabled and every undo entry point routes to the single muya history owner.

Constraints.Item: One history owner is chosen at plan time from the architectures in design-context.xml (recommendation: muya's snapshot history becomes the document history, source-pane commits enter through a history- aware path, CodeMirror's built-in history is disabled while the unified history is active). Whichever is chosen, R-2's behavior is the acceptance bar.

Muya core changes, if any, are limited to the commit/history path the plan enumerates, carry MODULE_CONTRACT/CHANGE_SUMMARY updates in the same bundle, and keep single-pane WYSIWYG undo byte-identical in behavior (existing muya undo e2e corners stay green).
Existing gates stay green and unweakened: npm test, renderer suites, e2e; the rewritten split-view.spec.ts corners must be at least as strict as before.

The working tree carries parallel active changes (C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY cursor plumbing in editor.vue, theme work in the same components); the plan runs grace lint --parallel-preflight before any write and reconciles observed-write overlaps instead of assuming them.
Scroll behavior on pane updates is owned by C-SPLIT-SCROLL-SYNC and is expected to land first; this change must not regress it.

No release or train admission follows from approval; version bumps and tags stay behind their separate owner instruction. English only in all committed artifacts. No new user-facing strings by design (pane-role hints, if the plan's UX corner demands them, ship as native copy in all ten locales).
